newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Huels AG eyes Taiwan wafer project - paper.
newsitem.headline: Huels AG eyes Taiwan wafer project - paper.

text.p: German chemical group Huels AG is planning a T$10 billion silicon venture in Taiwan with local partners China Steel and Formosa Plastics, a Taipei newspaper said on Tuesday.

The United Daily News, quoting unnamed officials from the government's Industrial Development Bureau, said Huels planned the move to meet Taiwan's growing market for silicon wafers, the basic building block of integrated circuits.
The report did not specify stakes of the venture among the local and foreign partners or give details of the project.
China Steel spokesman Cheung Leh-min declined to confirm or deny the Huels' report when reached by telephone.
"Nothing is for sure until it is finalised," he said.
Other executives could not be reached for comment.

Taisil Electronic Materials Corp, a venture of Taiwan's Asia Pacific Investment Co and Japan's Komatsu Electronics Metals Co Ltd, is the island's number two silicon wafer maker following a T$4.85 billion venture between China Steel and U.S.-based MEMC Electronic Materials.
Huels AG is a unit of German utility group Veba AG.
